newsitem.title: USA: Lawmaker faults U.S. Defense Dept. on magazine.
newsitem.headline: Lawmaker faults U.S. Defense Dept. on magazine.

text.p: A House lawmaker accused the Defence Department Wednesday of using taxpayer money for political aims and wasting money by funding a magazine that hailed its environmental programmes.

"When the entire federal government is looking for ways to save money, I find it objectionable to see precious Defence Department funds expended for this superfluous political publication," Representative William Clinger, R-Pennsylvania, said in a letter to Defence Secretary William Perry released Wednesday.

"Indeed, one might suspect that (the magazine) 'Today' is a political document printed at taxpayer's expense to advertise the self-described environmental successes of the Clinton administration," he said in the Oct. 8 letter.

Clinger, chairman of the House Government Reform and Oversight Committee, complained that the $120,000 for the magazine was unnecessary at a time when the department should be focusing on cleaning up its massive toxic waste sites.

Asked for reaction, Defence Department spokeswoman Nancy Burt said: "The 'Today' report was designed to provide a better understanding of the department's diverse environmental programmes and is a resource to both military and civilian communities for use in implementing their own environmental programmes."
